findings.F1: The short side earns nothing after fees. In the trending regime, short bars gain 0.000178 a day before fees and pay 0.000231 in fees, so they net -0.000053 over 3316 bars, while long bars net 0.001633 over 5173 bars (summed gain before fees 0.62 for shorts against 9.50 for longs).
findings.F2: The lower half of the 20-day range does not lead to a fall. On the trending 10-bar grid, bars with a negative forecast are followed by +0.0023 over 10 days (t 0.24, n 229), against +0.0274 (t 2.96, n 401) for bars with a positive forecast. Selling the low half bets on a fall that is not in the data.
findings.F3: Dropping the shorts would fix most of the falls. In an approximate rebuild of the book, long-only cuts the deepest fall from -0.340 to -0.243 and lifts Calmar from 0.46 to 0.70 and mean daily return from 0.000468 to 0.000486. Also skipping longs whose 30-day return is in the top fifth cuts the fall to -0.195 and lifts Calmar to 0.89 and Sharpe to 1.08, with the mean at 0.000476.
findings.F4: The drift fades when the coin has already run far. Long bars whose past 30-day return is in the top fifth (above +44%) gain -0.000168 a day. The middle fifth (+15% to +28%) gains 0.004317. On the trending 10-bar grid, the 10-day forward return is +0.053 (t 2.95, n 126) for 30-day returns of +18% to +36%, but only +0.013 (t 0.67, n 126) for the top fifth.
findings.F5: The worst moves come after extended runs while long. The worst 2% of position-bars are 73% long and all in the trending regime. On those bars the past 30-day return averages +30%, the past 10-day return +13% and the range position 0.70.
findings.F6: Volatility sizing shrinks the long position where the coin moves most. Long gain per bar falls from 0.0035 in the lowest 20-day-volatility fifth (mean position 0.96) to 0.0011 in the highest (mean position 0.31), even though the coin's next-day return is larger there (0.0041 against 0.0021). This holds the mean daily return below its bar.

ideas.idea: While a coin's close is above its 200-day average, the higher its close sits in its 20-day close range, the larger its rise over the next 10 days, except when its 30-day return is already extended, where the larger that 30-day return, the smaller the rise over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would scale a long by how near the close is to its 20-day high above the long average, and cut it back as the coin's 30-day run grows very large, which is where the book's deepest falls start.
ideas.name: near-high drift, extension fades

ideas.idea: While a coin's close is above its 200-day average, the higher its close sits in its 20-day close range, the larger its rise over the next 10 days, the coin still rising, only less, when its close sits in the lower half of that range.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold only longs graded by range position above the long average, and refuse shorts near the range low, since those pay fees for a fall that does not come.
ideas.name: near-high drift, long only

ideas.idea: While a coin's close is above its 200-day average, the larger its 30-day return up to a moderate gain, the larger its rise over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size longs above the long average by how strong, but not yet stretched, the coin's 30-day run is, expecting the payoff within about 10 days.
ideas.name: moderate momentum above average
